newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates steady in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates steady in active trade.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates were steady on Friday after slipping to lower levels this week thanks to improved supply, money market dealers said.
They said trade was more active due to end-of-week demand by the banking sector for corporate tax payments. Banks were also able to repay some old loans.
A total of fresh 62.7 million kuna was settled by 0900 GMT, mostly in call money loans at 10 percent.
Term rates remained unchanged at 11 percent for 12-day funds and 16 percent for two-month money.
Savings banks were charged 16 percent for 30-day and 19 percent for 90-day loans, one percentage point higher than the price for banks due to their perceived higher repayment risk.
Commercial banks completely repaid Lombard borrowing to the central bank, though some were expected to raise new loans by the end of the day.
Their total balances were put at 472 million kuna on Thursday and without shortfalls at any banks. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
